title: The Unofficial Tryouts
premise: Orsen Nystrom, the invisible statistician at Ashford Prep, has spent three years documenting the rigged athletic scholarship system in a private spreadsheet—until best friend Dev Okafor, the team's star and the only person who ever saw Orsen, vanishes the night before the final tryouts, leaving behind a set of keys to the athletic director's office. Following Dev's trail, Orsen discovers Dev had been quietly feeding evidence of the scholarship fraud to a local journalist, and that Dev's disappearance is no accident: the people he threatened have made him disappear to protect a booster-funded pipeline worth millions. Orsen must choose between publishing the truth—which exposes Dev's own complicity in taking bribes—and staying silent to preserve the friendship and Dev's reputation. Orsen publishes, Dev is found alive but disgraced, and the two must rebuild something honest from the wreckage, learning that belonging built on secrets was never belonging at all.
about_author: L. M. Nakamura is a former high school scorekeeper who spent six seasons in the bleachers of small-town gyms, collecting the statistics no one asked for and the stories everyone pretended not to see. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who keep receipts.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen catalogs the final weeks before graduation in precise numbers—days left, games logged, lies tallied in a hidden spreadsheet documenting rigged tryouts and bought scholarships. Dev is the only one who visits the stat booth. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of being invisible, and the first crack—Dev acting strange, distracted, defensive.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Dev misses their ritual diner night, then misses the final tryouts entirely. Orsen finds Dev's backpack abandoned behind the gym with a set of keys labeled 'AD—do not copy.' The school spins Dev's absence as 'family emergency.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as Orsen realizes no adult is going to look for Dev.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Say
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, intercut with flashbacks to Dev. Orsen runs the stats on Dev's last season and finds impossible patterns—performance dips timed to booster payments. The keys fit the athletic director's office, where Orsen finds shredded documents and a burner phone. Emotional beat: the sick thrill of proof colliding with the horror that Dev was involved.

chapters.title: The Booster Club
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen infiltrates a booster fundraiser disguised as a volunteer, hearing Athletic Director Marsh and a donor discuss 'the Okafor situation' as a solved problem. Orsen photographs everything but is nearly caught by teammate Priya, who covers for them—and starts asking her own questions. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose; the first ally.

chapters.title: Priya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, a scholarship player herself, reveals she suspected the fix—her roster spot came with strings. She and Orsen compare notes: Dev had approached her weeks ago asking what she'd do if the truth cost her everything. Emotional beat: two outsiders discovering belonging in shared risk, and Orsen's guilt over having kept Dev's secrets even from her.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following the burner phone's last text, Orsen finds reporter Camille Reyes, who confirms Dev was her source—and that Dev confessed to taking money, wanting to burn the whole system down including himself. Reyes warns Orsen: publishing exposes Dev. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—truth as betrayal, betrayal as love; Orsen must decide what loyalty actually means.

chapters.title: Marsh's Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Marsh corners Orsen with a deal: a full scholarship, a future, silence. He reveals Dev's disappearance was negotiated—Dev agreed to leave quietly, no police, no article, or the fraud lands on him alone. Emotional beat: corruption made personal and seductive; Orsen understands exactly how Dev got pulled in, and nearly takes the deal.

chapters.title: Where Dev Went
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, present tense. Dev, hiding at his uncle's place two states away, wrestles with the deal he made and the texts Orsen keeps sending. When he learns Marsh offered Orsen the same bargain, he realizes Orsen is in danger of disappearing the same way—erased by comfort. Emotional beat: Dev's shame and love; he chooses to come back, but he may already be too late.

chapters.title: Publish
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On graduation day, with Marsh threatening to pin everything on Dev, Orsen gives Reyes the spreadsheet, the photos, and the burner phone—accepting that the truth will wound Dev as much as it saves him. The story breaks; the school locks down; Marsh is suspended. Emotional beat: the climax—Orsen choosing justice over the friendship, at the exact moment Dev walks back into the gym to hear his name read aloud as a suspect.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.summary: Alternating Orsen and Dev POV. Weeks later, the investigation widens, Priya organizes players to testify, and Dev—stripped of his scholarship and reputation—shows up at the diner booth. No easy forgiveness: Dev is furious, then honest, then, finally, grateful. Orsen is no longer invisible, and neither is comfortable with it. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging rebuilt on truth, imperfect and chosen, as the two friends begin again.
